scope: Gmail account preparation for the existing Teable email-received IMAP trigger in all 11 locales

sources.title: Add Gmail to another email client
claims: Personal Gmail has IMAP permanently enabled from January 2025 and no Enable/Disable IMAP selector.
Use of a regular Google Account password by third-party clients is no longer supported.

sources.title: Sign in with app passwords
claims: Security-key-only verification, Advanced Protection, and organizational accounts may not offer app passwords.
Google provides the create/manage app passwords entry point at myaccount.google.com/apppasswords.
Changing the Google Account password revokes app passwords; each app password is shown only once and can be revoked.

sources.title: Turn POP & IMAP on or off for users
claims: Workspace administrators control IMAP availability and client restrictions.
Gmail Settings administrator privilege is required to manage this setting.
sources.source_caveat: The page retains legacy less-secure-app instructions. These are not repeated in the guide; use the current transition document for authentication requirements.

sources.title: Transition from less secure apps to OAuth
claims: Legacy main-password access is retired, with app passwords explicitly described as an exception.
Workspace users do not enable or disable IMAP in their own Gmail settings.

decisions: Replace obsolete personal Gmail IMAP toggle steps with account-specific access guidance.
Link directly to current Google account settings, avoiding retired Select App/Select Device selectors.
Remove screenshots tied to previous Google settings screens.
Keep existing new-unread-email trigger behavior documented in email-received-overview; make no new OAuth support claim for Teable.
Preserve all 55 published heading hashes as raw span aliases; keep the heading levels established by fix 14.
